title: Pay a toll or toll notice
summary: This page provides information on how to pay for tolls or toll notices incurred while using toll roads in NSW.
intro:
Motorists are required to pay to use toll roads in NSW.

If you use a toll road without an active toll account or pass you have 3 days to make payment arrangements with the toll road provider. This could include opening a tolling account or setting up a casual pass. Find out more at How to get an electronic tag or pass.

If you do not pay for the trip a toll notice will be issued and will include the toll charge plus an administration fee.

Before receiving a toll notice you may receive an 'unpaid toll reminder' email so you can pay your toll before the administration fee is added. Note that video matching fees may still apply at the time of payment.
who_can_apply: Motorists using toll roads in NSW
what_you_need: The vehicle licence plate number and state of registration

how_to_steps.text: Visit E-Toll to pay a toll or toll notice for using the Sydney Harbour Bridge or Sydney Harbour Tunnel.
Enter the vehicle details or the toll notice number.
Follow the prompts to complete your transaction.
call the toll notice payment line on 1300 883 114 (24-hour automated self-service payment) or
visit a Service NSW Centre (for the payment of toll notices only).
Visit Linkt to pay a toll or toll notice for using any other Sydney toll road (that is, any toll road other than Sydney Harbour Bridge or Sydney Harbour Tunnel).
Enter the vehicle details or the toll notice number.
Follow the prompts to complete your transaction.

faqs.q: What happens if I use a toll road without an active account or pass?
faqs.a: You have 3 days to make payment arrangements with the toll road provider. This could include opening a tolling account or setting up a casual pass.

faqs.q: What happens if I do not pay for the trip?
faqs.a: A toll notice will be issued, which will include the toll charge plus an administration fee. You may first receive an 'unpaid toll reminder' email.

faqs.q: How can I pay for a toll or toll notice?
faqs.a: You can pay by visiting E-Toll for the Sydney Harbour Bridge or Sydney Harbour Tunnel, visiting Linkt for other Sydney toll roads, calling Service NSW, or visiting a Service NSW Centre (for notices only).
